anchor_adjudication.reason: For a known rigid rotation model, pyGPlates can evaluate each plate's velocity at the same canonical boundary point; this removes the arbitrary-distance cell-anchor requirement for kinematic side velocities. evaluate both plate velocities at identical point/time interval
transform global vector into canonical local normal/tangent basis
record units, orientation convention, rotation-model identity, and uncertainty
validate left/right ordering against ARCANA edge orientation

shellset_input_gap_analysis.finding: ShellSet/SHELLS is materially closer to the thin-shell R6 problem than a 3-D mantle code, but cannot consume the ARCANA graph/rotation model by adapter alone. It needs a mechanical FEG/state and does not document taking ARCANA's plate-side velocity field as its primary solve input. The potential discrepancy between prescribed R6 kinematics and Shells force-balanced velocity is an unresolved model-interface/authority question.

questions.Q1_pygplates_eliminates_arbitrary_spatia: YES for PLATE_SIDE_KINEMATIC_STATE only. Evaluate both adjacent rigid rotation velocities at the same canonical boundary point. It does not establish material support away from boundary or any mechanical law; adapter orientation/unit proof is outstanding.
questions.Q2_shellset_consumes_arcana_topology_kin: NO evidence that it does. ShellSet uses its own spherical FE grid/fault network and predicts force-balanced velocity; ARCANA lacks solver state and its rotation/velocity relation to Shells output is unresolved. This is not merely a file format adapter.
questions.Q3_shellset_mandatory_vs_earth_calibrati: Documented model inputs include a node-wise spherical FE grid with surface elevation, crust/mantle-lithosphere thickness, densities, thermal structure and rheological parameters; fault elements/parameters if discrete faults are modeled. OrbData can produce some grid quantities under data/assumption-based algorithms and is optional when a suitable grid already exists. Earth geodetic velocities, stress azimuth, SKS, seafloor spreading, fault slip and seismicity datasets are OrbScore calibration/scoring evidence, not required simply to execute Shells. Exact minimal zero/simplified configuration has not been source/manual-qualified.
questions.Q4_gwb_can_provide_missing_initial_state: YES, as a materialization/provider: from explicit authored feature geometries, profiles and composition labels it can query temperature/composition in Cartesian or spherical domains. It cannot decide ARCANA boundary class, fault status, subduction, or values/authority.
questions.Q5_aspect_consume_gplates_velocity_and_g: Technically yes in principle: ASPECT documents GPlates as a prescribed boundary-velocity model and accepts temperature/composition initial conditions; an adapter must produce compatible mesh, GPlates data/model files and GWB fields. Tractable as an integration prototype, not ready as R6 production because model state/authority and 3-D global cost remain unresolved.
questions.Q6_underworld3_unique_capability: NO unique gap closure established versus ASPECT for R6. It offers Python/SymPy extensibility, PETSc FEM/PIC, curved coordinates and rich rheology, valuable for regional research, but the user must define physics and initial state.
questions.Q7_lamem_unique_capability: NO unique required gap closure established. It is a strong regional 3-D thermo-mechanical/geomechanical solver with marker-in-cell, staggered FD and visco-elasto-plastic rheology; global spherical production is not established by sources inspected.
questions.Q8_custom_patch_operator_retirement: YES, the current operator need not enter production if the selected specialist discretization natively solves the connected material domain/fault mechanics. Preserve its failure as diagnostic/history. A regional ARCANA coupler may still be needed for solver-domain boundaries, not to reimplement mechanics.
questions.Q9_exact_fields_before_any_mechanical_en: At minimum for any mechanical calculation: solver geometry/mesh and support; an explicitly selected governing equation/configuration; constitutive relation plus parameters; boundary conditions/loads with units/support/time; material density/structure as required by selected equations. For thermo-mechanical ShellSet/ASPECT/LaMEM cases also thermal state, compositional/material fields, lithosphere/crust layering as required. To claim fault accommodation, add authorized fault/process classes and fault/weak-zone geometry/law. There is no universally exact field list independent of engine/formulation.
questions.Q10_fields_producible_by_existing_tools: pyGPlates can derive rigid velocities/kinematic deformation from rotations/topology; GWB can materialize authored temperature/composition features; OrbData can derive Shells grid structure from datasets and stated assumptions; specialists calculate mechanical outputs after valid setup. No inspected tool supplies the missing ARCANA authority automatically.
questions.Q11_fields_requiring_authorial_initializ: If no suitable observation/provider authority is adopted: synthetic lithosphere/crust layering; thermal profiles; material composition/density relationships; rheology family and parameter distributions; tectonic boundary/fault classifications; weak zones; accepted BC/traction interpretation; event transition semantics. Values are not selected here.
questions.Q12_minimum_viable_toolchain: Candidate minimum is ARCANA canonical T0 + pyGPlates for identity-preserving geometry/side-velocity derivation + one mechanics specialist, with ShellSet/SHELLS the closest global thin-shell candidate and ASPECT the leading high-fidelity regional validator. GWB is optional and only needed if an approved model chooses feature-driven temperature/composition initialization. No toolchain is ready for execution/selection because ShellSet's kinematic/mechanical interface and required-state authority remain open; next stage should bind those inputs and interface before runtime qualification, not start an interval.

boundary_and_junction_findings.kinematic_triple_junction: pyGPlates can evaluate incident plate-side vectors at a shared point; analytical/vector closure can independently check consistency, but semantics and frame need adapter validation.

Native simultaneous closure is plausible but must be validated in a bounded qualification case; it does not replace event/classification authority.
